Targeted pass of a 506-page BREF. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 28). Main file: cement kiln fuel energy by kiln type (Table 1.18: precalciner, preheater, Lepol semi-dry, long dry, wet, shaft/special) with capacities; BAT kiln system 2 900-3 300 MJ/t (short-term test), derived annual range (+160-320) and waste-fuel plants (Sect. 1.4.2.1.1); Padeswood wet-to-precalciner example; EU clinker CO2 900-1 000 kg/t with the printed 62/38 % process/fuel split (derived rows); whole-plant electricity 90-150 kWh/t cement; fluidised bed cement kiln (emerging); cement waste-heat power (Slite steam cycle, Lengfurt ORC with capex/opex, generic EUR 0.8-1.2 million/MW). Lime: Table 2.23 heat and electricity, Table 2.15 capacity and Table 2.25 CO2 (process 0.785, combustion, total) for LRK, PRK, PFRK, ASK, MFSK, OK in one combined context; dolime CO2 (0.913); Norsk Hydro GSC dolime kiln; dead burned dolime; Austrian (Table 6.32) and Spanish (Table 6.33) national kiln data; Kraft pulp captive lime kiln capacities; hydrating and grinding electricity; emerging fluidised bed and flash calciner (descriptions only). Magnesia: 6-12 GJ/t, 75-180 kWh/t, process ~1 t CO2/t and combustion 0.4-1.3 t/t (total derived), fused magnesia 3 500-4 500 kWh/t. Flows: raw meal per t clinker, limestone per t lime, magnesia fuels (alternatives, not additive), oxygen, magnesite. _measures: cement kiln size, cyclone stages, fuel fineness, bypass, direct firing, VRM/HPGR vs ball mill, precalciner conversion and wet-to-dry costs, process control, lime HPGR and fabric filter savings. _other-values: BAT-AEL duplicates (Tables 4.1, 4.6), theoretical energies, sector shares, misprinted values. Not loaded: BAT-AELs and costs for dust, NOx, SOx, metals, PCDD/F, water, noise; waste-fuel quality tables; chart readings (Fig. 1.21). Heating-value basis never stated for energy consumption (fuel calorific values are given as net). Traps: (1) Table 2.23 footnote says heat is ~80 % of total energy, text says ~95 %; (2) Table 1.23 prints CO2 as 672 g/tcement (means kg); (3) magnesia reaction enthalpy printed 2 803 MJ/kg (means kJ/kg); (4) Lengfurt ORC 1.1 MW (p.108) vs 1.0 MW net (p.420); (5) Slite about 6 MW not stated electric or thermal, and its EUR 8 million excludes the turbine; (6) price years not stated except Slite (1999); (7) Table 1.18 precalciner max printed as <4 000, long dry up to 5 000, shaft and higher; (8) PFRK electricity 20-40 (Table 2.23) vs 20-41 (Table 2.19), PRK capacity 150-1 500 (Table 2.15) vs 100-1 500 (Table 2.22); (9) lime kiln ranges are per t lime or dolime without separation; (10) lime process CO2 factors are IPCC defaults.
